role.altitude: The talent agent keeps picking opportunities, pitching, chasing late payers, auditioning and talking with contacts; working out fees by hand, typing invoices, matching bank lines, digging up showreels and rewriting the same pitch shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping contract terms and client media in one register
Editing drafted pitches in their own voice
role.ambitious_version: An agent who knows every open fee and every client's best material at a glance and spends the day on deals.

tasks.short: Compute fees and commissions from contract terms, prepare, check and send invoices, match payments, chase late payers, and pay out the client's share to collect fees, commissions or other payments.

steps.what: Agent computes fees and commissions due according to contract terms
Agent prepares the invoice to the promoter or employer
Agent checks the final invoice against the contract
Agent sends the approved invoice to the promoter or employer
Agent matches incoming payments to invoices
Agent chases late payers by phone and mail
Agent works out the client's share after commission and prepares the payout
Agent checks the final payout: client, amount, commission and bank account
Agent releases the approved payout to the bank

approvals.approved_version: The invoice with amount, lines and addressee exactly as checked by the agent in s3 against the contract, sent once to the promoter's or employer's invoice address; any change needs a new check before sending.
The payout with client, amount after commission and bank account exactly as checked by the agent in s8, released once to the bank; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: Each deal's fee, commission rate and payment dates are entered once in a contract register linked to the accounting package, which computes what is due and when. The agent checks the invoice drafted from the register and sends that version. A bank feed matches payments by invoice number and lists what is overdue, so the agent chases from a list instead of reconciling a spreadsheet. Chasing payers stays personal. When a payment is matched, the package works out the client's share after commission and prepares the payout; the agent checks it and releases it to the bank.
tasks.previous_blocker: Terms sat in contract files and payments were reconciled in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Contract registers linked to accounting with bank feeds.
tasks.still_hard: Deals with bonuses or royalties that depend on later figures.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a promoter to pay without souring the relationship.

ambition.what: Check what is owed every week instead of at month end.

tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic and reconciling; chasing stays.

evidence.claim: Records apps and dashboards on accounting data handle reports, records and monitoring deterministically.

assumptions: Boundary: collecting payments; accounting statements for clients (task 12874) and managing clients' financial affairs (task 12871) are sibling tasks.
Priced here: the answer for sibling task 12871 does not cut the payout. s7 keeps 30 for deals with split or variable commission; the check and release keep their full time.
Input contract for s1: deal terms entered in the register when the contract is signed, under task 12869.
Checking and chasing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of deals with variable fees.

incremental.description: Agent enters deal terms in the register when signing.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of deals have variable or split fees the register cannot compute, so s1 and s7 keep 60 (35.7); high: mostly fixed fees computed from the register as designed (44.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify the opportunity and client, select samples, write the pitch, check it, send samples of clients' work and promotional material to potential employers, and follow up.

steps.what: Agent identifies the opportunity and decides which client to put forward
Agent selects samples of the client's work: showreel, photos and record
Agent writes the pitch message

loop.input: The client's profile and credits in the agency register and the opportunity brief.
loop.output: A draft pitch message naming the client's relevant credits.
loop.check: The agent checks that the pitch claims only what the client's profile and samples show and that it answers what the brief asks; every credit, statistic and award must match the profile; the agent rewrites the message in their own voice.
loop.stop: The agent keeps the pitch, or writes it by hand after two redrafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: Each brief asks for a different angle on the client.

steps.what: Agent checks the final pitch, samples and recipient
Agent sends the pitch with a link to the samples to the potential employer
Agent follows up with casting directors and sponsors

approvals.approved_version: The pitch text, the sample link and the recipient exactly as checked by the agent in s4, sent once to the named casting director or employer; any edit needs a new check before sending.

tasks.design: Choosing the opportunity and the client stays with the agent. Each client's current showreel, photos and credits sit in a tagged media library, so samples are picked in minutes and shared as a link that tracks opens, instead of searching folders and attaching large files. A drafting step writes the pitch from the client's profile and the brief, every credit matching the profile, and the agent rewrites it and sends that checked version. Follow-up calls stay personal. Samples are only shared as the client agreed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Material sat in scattered folders and pitches were written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Tagged media libraries with share links and drafting checked against client profiles.
tasks.still_hard: Briefs that want something the client has not done yet.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which casting director will take a call about an unknown name.

ambition.what: Pitch for more briefs a week with the same effort.

tasks.altitude: Less searching and writing; picking and following up stay.

reach.learn: Whether pitches arrive with the right material first time.

evidence.claim: A consultancy partly refunded a government report that cited non-existent sources, so drafted pitches are checked against the client's profile.
Drafting from approved sources with a named person signing works for letters and copy.

assumptions: Boundary: sending samples and pitches; developing contacts (task 12867) and scheduling engagements (task 12868) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: clients' current material kept in the media library by the agency.
Choosing, checking and follow-up keep their full time.
s3 keeps 75: the draft fills credits and sample details from the profile, but the agent writes the pitch in their own voice.
research_questions: Do more pitches lead to auditions?

incremental.description: Agent keeps client material in the library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the media library is not kept current, so samples are still searched for and s2 keeps 80, and the agent rewrites most drafts, so s3 keeps 90 (7.5); high: a current library and usable drafts as designed (16.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read trade press and newsletters, talk with contacts, track deals and rates, and judge what industry trends and deals mean for clients.

steps.what: Agent reads trade press, newsletters and deal announcements
Agent talks with contacts at events and by phone about deals
Agent records deals and going rates: in private notes today, in the agency's register after the change
Agent judges what industry trends and deals mean for their clients

tasks.design: News alerts on the agency's clients, competitors, productions and sponsors replace scanning every newsletter in full; the agent still reads what the alerts point to. Deals and rates go into the same register the agency uses for its own contracts, with fields for party, fee range and date, instead of a private spreadsheet; the agent still writes each entry, so this keeps its time. Talking with contacts and judging what it means stay with the agent.
tasks.previous_blocker: News came through many newsletters and deal notes sat in personal files.
tasks.enabler_now: Keyword news alerts and shared deal registers.
tasks.human_edge: Reading between the lines of what a promoter says over coffee.
tasks.altitude: Less scanning; contacts and judgement stay.

reach.learn: Whether shared rate notes help negotiations.

evidence.claim: Keyword news alerts and shared registers are standard tools.

assumptions: Boundary: keeping informed; developing contacts (task 12867) is a sibling task.
Talking with contacts, recording deals and judging keep their full time; recording in the register instead of notes is a first record, not a saving.
unknowns: How many newsletters the agent reads today.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: alerts miss many relevant items, so the agent still scans most newsletters and s1 keeps 85 (4.9); high: alerts point to what matters as designed (10.2).

tasks.short: Receive submissions through a form, screen reels and CVs, schedule auditions or interviews, conduct them to evaluate potential clients, and decide whether to sign.

steps.what: Applicant sends reel link, CV and category: by mail today, through the submission form after the change
Agent screens submitted reels and CVs
Agent schedules auditions or interviews: by mail back and forth today; after the change opens audition slots, writes the invitation and books applicants who do not use the page
Agent checks the final invitations: shortlisted applicants, audition details and the booking link
Agent sends the checked invitations to the shortlisted applicants
Shortlisted applicant picks an audition slot on the booking page
Agent conducts auditions or interviews to evaluate potential clients
Agent decides whether to sign the potential client

tasks.design: Applicants submit through a form on the agency site with a reel link, CV and category, so the agent screens one list sorted by category instead of opening mails and attachments; no software scores or ranks applicants. Shortlisted applicants pick an audition slot from a booking page. Auditions, interviews and the decision to sign stay with the agent.

approvals.approved_version: The audition invitation with date range, place and booking link exactly as checked by the agent in s3b, sent once to the shortlisted applicants on the checked list; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Submissions arrived by mail in every format.
tasks.still_hard: Talent that does not show well on a reel.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing presence in the room that a reel misses.
tasks.altitude: Less sorting and scheduling; judging talent stays.

evidence.claim: Solely automated decisions with significant effect need a legal basis and human intervention, so no score decides here.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating potential clients; negotiating contracts (task 12869) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2: about 70% of applicants use the form; mailed submissions are added by hand; s2 is priced at that share.
Applicants' time on the form is shown in s1 and is about what a mail took.
Auditions and the decision keep their full time. s2 keeps 80: opening mails and attachments drops, but watching reels and reading CVs stays. Applicants' slot booking is shown in s6.
research_questions: Do applicants get an answer sooner?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of applicants use the form, so s2 keeps 90, and many still mail about dates, so s3 keeps 70 (6.1); high: about 70% use the form and the booking page as designed (12.6).
